story: AIDEA's October 21st board creates a $75 million fiber investment subsidiary while separately putting $25 million into microreactor company NuCube, with updates on DeepGreen's Cook Inlet subsea data center and Anchorage's surveillance ordinance

claims.claim: The AIDEA board voted unanimously on October 21st to adopt Resolution G26-11.
claims.verbatim: voted unanimously to adopt Resolution No. G26-11
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (press release 20-2026)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py. The release gives the meeting as 'Wednesday, October 21, 2026'. The signed resolution text itself doesn't record the vote tally, so the word unanimous rests on AIDEA's release. Must Read Alaska republished the release on October 26th with the same wording ('Press release provided by AIDEA').

claims.claim: Resolution G26-11 creates Northstar Fiber Development LLC as a wholly owned AIDEA subsidiary with AIDEA as its sole member.
claims.verbatim: as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Authority with the Authority as its sole member
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed Resolution G26-11)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py, Section 1. The executive director may instead use the name Alaska Northstar Network Development LLC or another name, and may form the company in Alaska or Delaware.

claims.claim: Resolution G26-11 caps the subsidiary's capitalization at $75 million.
claims.verbatim: SUBSIDIARY IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $75,000,000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed Resolution G26-11)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py, title block. The press release says 'up to $75 million'. NOT THE SAME $75 MILLION as NuCube's '$75 million Minimum Cash Condition' (C53). That is an unrelated SPAC closing condition, so the deck must not mix the two up.

claims.claim: The resolution authorizes moving up to $75 million out of AIDEA's Revolving Fund to the subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: approves the transfer of up to $75,000,000 from the Revolving Fund
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed Resolution G26-11)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py, Section 4. The full text reads 'from the Revolving Fund (or such other fund as may be appropriate under AS 44.88.060)', so the deck should hedge with 'from the Revolving Fund or another appropriate fund'. Each transfer needs the CFO to certify the funds are available.

claims.verbatim: Transfers shall be staged. Until the Executive Director approves a qualifying investment under Section 5, transfers shall be limited to amounts
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed Resolution G26-11)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py, Section 4. The sentence goes on 'the Chief Financial Officer certifies as necessary for the formation, operation, and professional services of NFD LLC.' Money for an investment stays in the Revolving Fund until that investment needs it.

claims.claim: The $75 million is the aggregate ceiling for all transfers and commitments under the resolution and is not additive.
claims.verbatim: The $75,000,000 amount is the aggregate ceiling for all transfers and commitments under this Resolution, is not additive
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed Resolution G26-11)
claims.notes: Text via fetch_pdf_text.py, Section 5. The Section 4 transfer and the Section 5 commitment authority are not two separate $75 million amounts.

One drafting quirk: (g) ends with a period, and (h) starts as a separate sentence fragment ('(h) requiring written confirmation from external counsel...'), but it is still labeled as one of the items. On the page the opening sentence ends with a colon, and the verbatim stops before it. Section 5 refers to these as 'each condition in the first paragraph of Section 9'.

Where each condition is covered: (i) C93, (ii) C23, (iii) C94, (iv) C95, (v) C96 plus C22, (vi) C97, (vii) C24, (viii) C98. C24 already covers (vii), so it gets no new claim.

killed.claim: The FCC cleared GCI's roughly $310 million purchase of Quintillion in an order released October 20th.
killed.why: Single secondary source (Broadband Breakfast, October 26th). The article doesn't link the FCC order. fcc.gov returned 403, the GCI newsroom returned 404, and news.gci.com carries no October 2026 item. No primary or second independent source found, so killed under the single-source rule.
